messages.text:
"CREATE: COLLECT A JUNKYARD

Create a complete, playable Roblox multiplayer simulator game called COLLECT A JUNKYARD.

IMPORTANT: The gameplay should be inspired by Collect a Stud, but use an original junkyard collection theme, original models, and original map design.

1. MAIN GAMEPLAY

- Players spawn in their own physical junkyard base.
- Junk items spawn on a central conveyor belt and in different map zones.
- Players collect junk items.
- Players bring junk back to their own bases.
- Place junk on designated slots.
- Each placed junk item generates passive Cash.
- Collect Cash from the items.
- Buy better and rarer junk.
- Expand and upgrade your base.
- Unlock new map zones.

2. HUGE OPEN WORLD MAP

Build a large, detailed map with six separate rarity zones:

COMMON ZONE:
Plastic bottles, cans, old tires, scrap wood.

UNCOMMON ZONE:
Metal pipes, scrap machines, old equipment.

RARE ZONE:
Car engines, batteries, copper wires, computer parts.

EPIC ZONE:
Advanced machinery, powerful metal scrap, special engines.

LEGENDARY ZONE:
Golden cars, legendary machines, golden scrap bots.

MYTHICAL ZONE:
Futuristic scrap, glowing machines, extremely rare collectibles.

Each zone must have:

- Unique environment.
- Unique decorations.
- Unique collectible junk.
- Different spawn chances.
- Different income values.
- Zone name signs.
- Unlockable gates.
- Teleport points.

3. PLAYER BASE SYSTEM

- Create 8 physical player bases.
- Each player automatically receives one available base.
- Display the player's username on their base.
- Each base has multiple junk placement slots.
- Junk generates passive income.
- Allow players to upgrade and expand their bases.
- Prevent other players from taking ownership of bases.

4. JUNK COLLECTION SYSTEM

Create collectible junk with different rarities:

- Common
- Uncommon
- Rare
- Epic
- Legendary
- Mythical

Add pickup animations, collection effects, rarity colors, and item names.

5. SHOP SYSTEM

Create a working shop where players can purchase junk, upgrades, and special items.

6. ECONOMY SYSTEM

Main currency: CASH

Add:

- Cash leaderboard.
- Passive income.
- Collect income buttons.
- Purchase system.
- Upgrade prices.
- Rebirth rewards.

7. BASE UPGRADES

- More placement slots.
- Higher income multipliers.
- Faster collection.
- Better storage.
- New base sections.
- Special decorations.

8. ADDITIONAL SYSTEMS

- Inventory GUI.
- Trading system.
- Pet system.
- Daily rewards.
- Rebirth system.
- Data saving.
- Player leaderboard.
- Secret junk collectibles.
- Limited-time events.

9. USER INTERFACE

Create a clean, modern Roblox simulator GUI.

Include:

- Cash display.
- Inventory.
- Shop.
- Upgrade menu.
- Rebirth button.
- Zone teleport menu.
- Settings.
- Daily rewards.
- Pet inventory.

All buttons must work.

10. MAP DESIGN

Create a huge open-world junkyard with:

- Central conveyor belt.
- Six rarity zones.
- Eight player bases.
- Roads and bridges.
- Industrial factories.
- Abandoned cars.
- Scrap mountains.
- Recycling machines.
- Secret areas.
- Shops and upgrade stations.

11. MULTIPLAYER

- Support multiple players.
- Give every player their own base.
- Keep player inventories separate.
- Make trading functional.
- Make income and collection work correctly for each player.

12. SAVE SYSTEM

Save:

- Cash.
- Inventory.
- Owned junk.
- Base upgrades.
- Unlocked zones.
- Rebirth progress.
- Pets.

FINAL REQUIREMENTS

Make the game fully playable, not just a map or visual demonstration.

Build the map, bases, collectible junk, conveyor belt, GUI, shops, rarity zones, upgrades, and working gameplay systems.

Ensure all systems work together, are multiplayer compatible, and are optimized.

Prioritize a working playable game over decorative features. Do not leave important buttons or systems non-functional.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"
